headline: Bolsonaro edges Lula into a run-off; US pulls bombers from RAF Fairford; AfD softens its euro-exit line.

stories.title: Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula in Brazil’s first round; run-off on 25 October
facts: With ~99% counted: Flávio Bolsonaro ~47.0% vs Lula ~45.2% of valid votes (BBC); neither cleared 50%, so the two meet again on 25 Oct.
Folha: the ~2-point gap is the narrowest first-round margin since redemocratisation; every run-off since 1989 was won by the first-round leader.
Private polls had Lula ahead by ~3 points; Reuters says the upset may lift Brazil’s currency and stocks on the business-friendly challenger.
Lula called the result “unexpected” and said a new campaign starts Monday; Bolsonaro, son of jailed ex-president Jair, said he was “very happy”.
stories.whyItMatters: A Bolsonaro win would extend the run of Trump-aligned right-wing governments across Latin America to its largest economy.

image.alt: A composite image shows Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva, wearing a grey suit jacket and a burgundy tie, at the left, and Flávio Bolsonaro, wearing a light green shirt but no tie, speaking into a microphone.

via.label: The New York Times on X

stories.title: US pulls all bombers out of RAF Fairford after suspected terror plot
facts: Pentagon confirmed Sunday that every US bomber deployed to the Gloucestershire base has returned to home stations; NBC counts at least 12, some fresh rotations.
Trigger: 27 Sep police stop of three “suspicious vehicles” near the base; six men arrested on terror suspicion, all released on bail.
PM Andy Burnham cited “strong indications” Iran played a part; Tehran denies it. The base has been used for US strikes on Iran.
stories.whyItMatters: Withdrawing a whole bomber force from a key European staging base is an unusually visible security response to a plot on allied soil.

image.alt: A Rockwell B1 Lancer heavy bomber takes off

stories.title: AfD strategy paper drops immediate euro and EU exit in favour of “reform first”
facts: BILD obtained a paper discussed 29 Sep by AfD MEPs, Bundestag and Landtag members: no more immediate exit from the euro system.
Demands instead: end “indirect ECB state financing”, settle TARGET balances, sovereign-insolvency rules, opt-outs (migration, social, fiscal), a “Bund souveräner Nationen”.
Also: abolish direct election of the European Parliament and send delegates from national parliaments; if reforms fail, the people should decide Germany’s path.
stories.whyItMatters: Exit stays in the programme as a fallback, but moving it off the front lets the AfD argue Europe policy without dropping its sovereignty line.

stories.title: Linke files emergency motion in Karlsruhe over Reiche’s ministry video
facts: Target: an Economy Ministry Instagram clip of a 23 Sep speech in which Reiche called the Linke’s Berlin win dangerous for the capital and Germany as an investment location.
The clip accuses the party of talking about expropriation and living antisemitism openly; a lawyer’s deadline to remove it by 29 Sep passed with the video still up.
Argument: the minister broke the state-organ neutrality rule and the Linke’s right to equal political competition — part of a “systematic campaign” by the CDU.

stories.title: Dodik claims victory as nationalists top Bosnia’s low-turnout election
facts: Dodik ally Željka Cvijanović leads the Serb seat of the three-way presidency with >55% (~90% counted); Dodik himself is banned from office for six years.
Bosniak incumbent Denis Bećirović and Croat nationalist Darijana Filipović also take their seats; Dodik-backed Savo Minić wins the Republika Srpska presidency.
Turnout ~42%, roughly 10 points below 2022. Dodik thanked Trump’s “magnificent victory” and Putin: “No one should ask us to change our politics.”
stories.whyItMatters: An SNSD hold keeps the secessionist pressure and the reform deadlock that stall Bosnia’s EU path.

stories.title: Suspected pneumonic plague death at Irkutsk anti-plague institute; ~200 under observation
facts: A 28-year-old lab technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died; local media and a regional governor raised plague.
Rospotrebnadzor calls it “pneumonia of unknown aetiology” and says expanded tests found no organisms tied to her work.
US State Department is monitoring with the CDC and urged Moscow to share information “quickly and openly”; reports say nearly 200 people are under medical observation.

image.alt: Russian lab worker dies of suspected plague in Siberia; US monitoring case

stories.title: Probe finds intruders reached the propulsion system of supertanker VL Prosperity
facts: Bloomberg (via heise): FBI and US Coast Guard found evidence attackers gained access to the tanker’s drive system; who and how is still under investigation.
The fully laden ship lost communications near Gibraltar en route from Egypt to Galveston and was boarded in late August; it still sits off Texas.
US authorities have reportedly flagged nearly 20 vessels worldwide and require early notice if one heads for a US port.

stories.title: Up to 500 French lycées shut Monday as student protests turn violent
facts: Education Minister Geffray: lessons totally or partly suspended at 400–500 high schools; >1/3 of Île-de-France’s 468 closed; more protests Tuesday.
Since 17 Sep: 24 schools burned or ransacked, 78 staff hurt, >5,000 arrests (85% minors); pupils protest teacher absences, long days, run-down, overheated buildings.
PM Lecornu told regions to fill vacant posts and called a Tuesday meeting on school renovation; Amnesty France calls policing “disproportionate”.

facts.text: FlyDubai 1073: WSJ details missed chances in three countries — Oman had grounded the co-pilot over radical views, FlyDubai hired him without checking, Israel didn’t vet crews.
Medevac jet Heartbeat 104 (Bermuda→Boston) lost off Nantucket; Coast Guard ended the search and Latitude Air Ambulance says all six aboard are presumed dead.
Nebraska: copy-pasting “redacted” boxes in Google data-center filings exposed figures, e.g. Lincoln site 52.65 MW peak and ~13M gallons of water a year.
Gurman via MacRumors: Apple reportedly planning an event on 13 Oct (smart-home hub, HomePod mini, Apple TV expected); no invite yet.
OpenAI starts an essay series on the post-AGI economy: “The eternal complement” argues most machine intelligence may end up doing the boring execution work.

facts.text: 49ers beat the Broncos 24-14 to stay unbeaten; Purdy 19/30, 218 yds, 2 TD, and Kittle’s 56-yard TD with 2:15 left sealed it.
49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk left with a knee injury; Shanahan says “probably” a sprain, ACL initially looks intact, more tests pending.
Warriors drop the preseason opener 104-101 to the Clippers in Honolulu.

A browser-native classic VB6 IDE (HN, 150 pts).
Guillermo Rauch praises Go’s simplicity and fast feedback loops “for a human world”; James Ward’s unfollow reply over Go’s error handling sparked the thread.
